# shell

Interactive shell baseline: locale, editor/pager, vi keybindings, unlimited shared history, and a few generic command helpers.

---

## `shell_get_browser`

Print the browser command this machine should use. Honours $BROWSER and falls back to the first graphical browser found.

**Usage**

```sh
shell_get_browser
```

**Examples**

```sh
$(shell_get_browser) https://example.com
```

**OS** any &nbsp;·&nbsp; **Source** [`modules/common/shell.sh:134`](../../modules/common/shell.sh#L134)

## `shell_get_editor`

Print the editor command this machine should use. Honours $EDITOR and falls back to emacs. Other modules call this instead of hardcoding a name.

**Usage**

```sh
shell_get_editor
```

**Examples**

```sh
$(shell_get_editor) ~/notes.org
```

**OS** any &nbsp;·&nbsp; **Source** [`modules/common/shell.sh:125`](../../modules/common/shell.sh#L125)

## `shell_retry`

Re-run a command until it succeeds, at most N times (default: forever). Rescued from the old pacman.sh `try`, which was named after a real binary and — fatally for a sourced file — called `exit` on success, killing the interactive shell it was invoked from.

**Usage**

```sh
shell_retry [count] <command> [args...]
```

**Examples**

```sh
shell_retry 5 curl -fsS https://example.com
shell_retry ping -c1 gateway
```

**OS** any &nbsp;·&nbsp; **Source** [`modules/common/shell.sh:159`](../../modules/common/shell.sh#L159)

## `shell_serve_http`

Serve the current directory over HTTP. Salvaged from rhoit/rho.sh, whose other entries all shadowed real binaries and were retired.

**Usage**

```sh
shell_serve_http [port]
```

**Examples**

```sh
shell_serve_http 8000
```

**Requires** `python3`

**OS** any &nbsp;·&nbsp; **Source** [`modules/common/shell.sh:197`](../../modules/common/shell.sh#L197)

## `shell_setup_history`

Configure effectively unlimited, timestamped, cross-session shell history for whichever shell is running. Idempotent — safe to call again after re-sourcing.

**Usage**

```sh
shell_setup_history
```

**Examples**

```sh
shell_setup_history
```

**OS** any &nbsp;·&nbsp; **Source** [`modules/common/shell.sh:61`](../../modules/common/shell.sh#L61)

## `shell_time_command`

Time a command in whole seconds without needing bc or GNU date.

**Usage**

```sh
shell_time_command <command> [args...]
```

**Examples**

```sh
shell_time_command sleep 2
```

**OS** any &nbsp;·&nbsp; **Source** [`modules/common/shell.sh:180`](../../modules/common/shell.sh#L180)
